=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-side review of the Seller's update and Disclosure Letter

**Scope:** I've reviewed only the Seller's summary of positions and the Disclosure Letter. I haven't seen the SPA text or the underlying DD-002 to DD-012 documents, so the points below need checking against those.

**Overall view:** The package is not "fair and balanced". Individually, several positions are aggressive. Combined, they leave the Buyer with almost no recourse for the known problems. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter also contradicts its cover note on several points (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses). We should not accept the "negotiated positions" label. Please confirm internally that none of these was actually agreed in earlier rounds.

## Tier 1: Structural issues (these undermine the whole risk allocation)

**1. Limitations applied to everything (cl 12.3/13, 9.3/12.8/20.5)**
- The Seller wants the cap, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance wording to apply to "all Claims of any nature" and "unless expressly stated otherwise".
- On that drafting, they would catch title and capacity claims, tax, specific indemnities and fraud.
- Title and capacity warranties should be capped at the full price, with no de minimis or basket, and a long time limit (6 years is the NSW contract limitation period and a sensible anchor).
- Tax claims should run for the ATO amendment period plus a buffer.
- Specific indemnities should sit outside all caps, thresholds and time limits.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and dishonesty must be uncapped. Non-reliance and exclusive-remedy wording must not exclude fraud or misleading-conduct claims. The Buyer should also keep injunctive relief, specific performance and a pre-Completion termination right.

**2. General disclosure plus constructive knowledge (Sch 7, DL 1.1–1.2, cl 8.3)**
- Disclosing the whole data room and public registers, together with no claim for anything "discoverable", would neutralise most warranties.
- Replace this with specific disclosure only, against identified warranties, with fair-disclosure detail.
- Delete DL 1.2 and the "discoverable" limb of cl 8.3. Any knowledge qualifier should be limited to the actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals. It should not apply to indemnities, title or fraud.
- The data room cut-off was 22 September 2026. Require updated disclosure and a bring-down at Completion. Post-signing disclosure must not cure breaches.
- DL 1.4 ("no admission") is acceptable only if it doesn't qualify the indemnities.

**3. Cap and thresholds (cl 12.1/12.2)**
- A cap of AUD 4.8m (20%) is within a negotiable range for general warranties. But the known items below total roughly AUD 4.1m before the data incident and Bluefen are even counted, so the cap cannot be the Buyer's main protection for them.
- The de minimis of AUD 25k and basket of AUD 250k, recoverable only in excess, is a deductible. Push for a tipping basket (first dollar), a lower de minimis, and aggregation of related claims.
- Consider 24 months for general claims in place of 18, so that two reporting cycles are covered.
- Given the Seller is a holding company, ask for a retention or escrow, or a guarantee, so that the Buyer can actually recover.

## Tier 2: Specific deal-critical items

**4. Bluefen (about AUD 3.6m, about 30% of FY26 revenue)**
- The cover note says the consent is "addressed", but DL §2 admits there is no final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- "Reasonable endeavours" and "satisfied on delivery of written consent" would let the Seller deliver a consent carrying onerous conditions.
- Make it a condition precedent: written consent that is unconditional, or conditional only on terms acceptable to the Buyer and satisfied. Only the Buyer may waive it. Include a long-stop date and a termination right, and give the Buyer a right to participate in the approach.
- On a rough pro-rata of the price to revenue (about 2x), the revenue at risk is worth around AUD 7m. That is illustrative only, but it supports a price adjustment or deferred consideration if the consent is waived.

**5. Riverlark (about AUD 3.2m)**
- A release "following Completion" breaches the debt-free premise. DL §3 confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge is provided.
- Require a payout letter, with the payout amount deducted from the price and paid directly to the lender through the funds flow. Discharge and PPSR releases should be delivered at Completion, including any share security.
- Check the cl 8.1 change-control and default consequences, and break costs.

**6. Completion bonuses (AUD 420k, DD-005)**
- These are Company liabilities triggered by Completion, so the Buyer would bear them in practice. Calling them "a matter for the Seller" while leaving them out of the funds flow is a cost-shift.
- Treat them as Transaction Costs/debt-like items deducted from the price, plus employer on-costs (superannuation and NSW payroll tax; the tax advisers should quantify these).
- If the Buyer wants a retention element, the continued-employment condition can be negotiated separately.

**7. Ironquay IP (AUD 180k, DD-004/DD-010)**
- The real risk is title to the SOW3 Project Materials, which only transfer on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee (cl 7.3). It is not the AUD 180k itself. The Seller's indemnity covers only the payment.
- The AUD 180k is also unverified. DL §4 says there is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- Require, as a Completion deliverable, evidence of cleared payment and a signed confirmatory assignment.
- Failing that, require a wider uncapped indemnity covering all losses from the IP chain: rebuild or licence costs, injunctions, and customer claims.
- Make IP title a fundamental warranty.

**8. DD-006 data incident (about 1,240 records)**
- "Not expected to be material" is unsupported. DL §6 says access, scope and notification are all unresolved.
- The Notifiable Data Breaches scheme requires an assessment within 30 days of suspecting an eligible breach. More than 6 weeks have passed since the 22 September status, so ask whether the assessment was completed and when. The Company likely turns over well above the small-business threshold, but please confirm that.
- Require the forensic and assessment materials, a covenant to complete the assessment and notify where required (with the Buyer's input), and no admissions or regulator contact without Buyer consent.
- Require a specific uncapped indemnity for regulatory, notification, remediation and customer-claim costs. Also check customer contracts for their own breach-notice obligations, and check insurance notification.

**9. Title (DD-012)**
- The company's own register is not independent proof. Require a full title and capacity warranty, plus an ASIC extract, a PPSR search for security over the shares, and a check of the constitution for pre-emption or transfer restrictions.
- Also require confirmation that there are no options, convertible instruments or shareholder agreements, board and Seller approvals for the sale, and a share transfer form at Completion.

## Tier 3: Verify and tighten

- **Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k):** The Seller asserts they are ordinary course, but DL §8 won't confirm that they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. They are three identical AUD 110k items, which is a pattern worth testing (for example, contract-splitting or pre-Completion commitments). Obtain the contracts. Treat any prepaid or non-terminable commitments as debt-like, and require Buyer consent for renewals in the interim period.
- **Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** The disclosures are hedged ("does not state"). Check the actual clauses for deemed-assignment or change-of-control triggers and notice timing. Seek a warranty that no consents or notices are required other than those scheduled.
- **Tax and IP "settled":** Reject this. Require a pre-Completion tax indemnity and covenant, and tax and IP warranties on the longer time limits above.

## Summary of recommendations

1. Reject uniform limitations. Carve out title, capacity, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. Fundamental warranties are capped at the full price, with no thresholds and a long tail.
2. Delete the general data-room disclosure and the "discoverable" knowledge bar. Specific disclosure only, with an updated bring-down.
3. Counter on the basket (tipping), de minimis and time limit. Seek a retention, escrow or guarantee.
4. Bluefen: a Buyer-controlled condition precedent, a firm consent obligation, a long-stop date, and price protection if waived.
5. Riverlark: pay out and discharge at Completion through the funds flow.
6. Treat the AUD 420k bonuses plus on-costs as a price deduction.
7. Ironquay: cleared payment plus assignment at Completion, or a broad specific indemnity.
8. Data incident: obtain the assessment materials, add a covenant and a specific uncapped indemnity, and control communications.
9. Title: independent verification and full fundamental warranties.
10. Sandbar, lease and Mossvale: confirm facts from the source documents, then adjust the price or covenants as needed.

**Next steps:** Our next step is to review the actual SPA clause text and DD-002 to DD-012. Please also tell me whether any of the "key negotiated positions" was genuinely agreed, so that I can mark up the SPA and prepare a response letter and a price-adjustment schedule.
